worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.summary: The quickest pounce, with current cutting the rhythm at the moment of contact: the bite deals damage and may paralyze the target; biting an already paralyzed target makes this contact's arcs brighter, but settles only the main damage and adds no root. A hard bite can also wince the target. Overload style paralyzes easier and longer; point-strike style hits harder.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.use.2: Wince the target and cut off what it is doing
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.descriptio: The bite deals about %1$s contact and bite damage over a fang radius of %2$s blocks; the target's defence, type matchup and crits are settled on impact.
A hit has a %1$s chance to run current through the target, paralyzing it for %2$s (half movement speed, a 25%% chance for its actions to fail).
If the target was already paralyzed when bitten, this contact's arcs are denser and brighter, but no root or other extra control is added, and only the main damage settles.
A hit has a %1$s chance to wince the target, interrupting interruptible actions; while flinching for %2$s it cannot start new moves or make ordinary attacks.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.overload.o: Overload style: easier and longer paralysis, but a lighter bite and a longer cooldown.
Point-strike style: a heavier bite and a faster cycle, but shorter paralysis.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.timing: Range %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, cooldown %4$s s, costing %5$s PP.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.growth.0: From level %1$s the bite power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.growth.1: From level %1$s the bite power rises to %2$s and the paralysis chance to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.thunderfang.preference: On: paralysis chance +12%%, paralysis duration x1.2, but bite power x0.88 and cooldown +4 ticks, for control. Off (point strike): a heavier bite and a faster cycle, but shorter paralysis.
Beyond this distance the user closes in first. The thunder fang reach is short, so a large value often still cannot connect.
